position_in_era.primary_genre_lineage: post-bop jazz piano × flamenco compás (founding flamenco-piano methodology)
position_in_era.historical_role: The flamenco-piano methodology that Dorantes' Orobroy steps into and reshapes. Domínguez is the Cádiz-born pianist who openly declared Bill Evans and Paco de Lucía as his two principal influences and built a piano language fluent in tangos, bulerías, alegrías, soleás. *Chano* (1993) and the later Blue Note album *Flamenco Sketches* (2012, Grammy-nominated) bracket the era. He is the methodological elder brother to Dorantes' translation aesthetic — same materials, slightly earlier in the timeline.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Numerous albums across Nuba, Sunnyside, and Blue Note labels; *Flamenco Sketches* (2012) was nominated for a Grammy and reframes Miles Davis's *Kind of Blue* through flamenco compás.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Self-described chain of influence: Mahavishnu Orchestra and Weather Report → Bill Evans and Thelonious Monk → Paco de Lucía. The Bill Evans / Paco de Lucía pairing is the public methodological signature of his work and the closest documented prior precedent to Dorantes' aesthetic.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Cádiz origin (Andalusian flamenco heartland) plus the international jazz circuit (Blue Note, JAZZBaltica, etc.).
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Acoustic piano in jazz trio / quartet contexts, with palmas and cajón frequently joining; compás-based phrasing applied to standard jazz-piano voicings.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: *Chano* (1993) is generally cited as the first major flamenco-jazz piano album by a flamenco-rooted pianist; *Flamenco Sketches* (Blue Note, 2012) earned the project international jazz-press visibility.
